note_on_pages: The assignment itself is a plain-text markdown file (input/hw2_instruction.md), not a PDF/Word document, so ingest produced NO page PNGs for it -- only ingest/pages/hw2_instruction/alltext.txt. There are no figures in the assignment. The only document with rendered pages is PaperList.xlsx (6 rendered pages + csv export), which is needed by p5 only.

problems.title: Ex. 2.1 Schedule diagrams: Round-Robin, FIFO, SJF
problems.anchor_text: Ex. 2.1 | (15pts) Draw schedule diagrams of the following task set for Round-Robin, First-in-first-out (FIFO), and Shortest job first (SJF)
problems.grouped_with_reason: The three diagrams share one task set and one set of tie-breaking conventions; splitting them would risk three workers using three different conventions for the same task set.

problems.title: Ex. 2.2 + Ex. 2.3 Process creation, and a fork()/exec() program
problems.anchor_text: Ex. 2.2 | (5pts) The following shows three different ways a process can be created. ... Ex. 2.3 | (5pts) Write a small program that uses fork() and exec() to run the ls command.
subparts: 2.2: explain why case 3 (a running process calling fork()) subsumes cases 1 and 2
2.3: write a small C program using fork() and exec() to run ls
problems.grouped_with_reason: 2.2 argues that every process creation reduces to an existing process calling fork()+exec(); 2.3 is that exact mechanism written out as a program. One worker keeps the argument and the code consistent (same fork/exec/wait shape).

problems.title: Ex. 2.4 Why a thread context switch is cheaper than a process context switch
problems.anchor_text: Ex. 2.4 | (5pts) The amount of time that takes to make a context-switch between threads versus that of between processes is much shorter. Explain why.

problems.title: Ex. 2.5 + Ex. 2.6 Pseudo-code for fork/exec/waitpid/exit, and zombie processes
problems.anchor_text: Ex. 2.5 | (20pts) Write a pseudo-code for exec(), fork(), waitpid(), and exit() system calls. ... Ex. 2.6 | (5pts) In Unix, there is a category of processes called zombie process. What are these?
subparts: 2.5: pseudo-code for fork() (2.5), exec() (2.5), waitpid() (2.5), exit() (2.5)
2.5: explanation of how the four calls inter-relate (2.5)
problems.grouped_with_reason: A zombie is precisely the state that the exit() pseudo-code leaves a child in and that waitpid() reaps. Written by two workers the two answers would almost certainly describe the exit/wait handshake differently; written by one they reinforce each other and 2.6 can point at the pseudo-code.

subparts: Paper 2-1 Rate Monotonic vs. EDF: Judgment Day (7.5)
problems.grouped_with_reason: One exercise, three papers; a single worker keeps the three critiques in one voice and avoids two workers picking the same paper.

problems.title: Ex. 2.8 Search for, summarize and critique three scheduling papers not on the list
problems.anchor_text: Ex. 2.8 | (22.5pts) Search for three papers on the topic of 'Scheduling'. Read, summarize, and critically judge them.
problems.grouped_with_reason: One exercise, three papers; kept together for the same reason as p5. Must not reuse any paper on the course list (those belong to Ex. 2.7).
